title: Designing a Halfpipe for Advanced Snurfers

source.pdf_page_offset_note: PDF page 1 is the title and abstract; PDF pages 2-24 correspond to printed body pages 1-23.

context_sources.use: Official Problem A summary: maximize vertical air, tailor shape for other requirements such as twist, and determine practical-course tradeoffs.
Official designation of control 12149 as Outstanding Winner and MAA Award recipient.

limitations: All 24 pages were rendered at 144 DPI and visually reviewed; equations, results, code, and appendix tables received full-resolution inspection.
Several mathematical glyphs are imperfect in text extraction, so equations were verified against rendered pages.
The appendix prints source code but provides no standalone file, compiler flags, build instructions, raw output, or executable artifact.
Official context verifies the MAA Award but contains no causal judge commentary.

required_outputs: Design a half-pipe shape maximizing vertical distance above the coping.
Tailor the shape for another performance objective such as twist.
Determine tradeoffs for a practical course.
paper_interpretation: Use an energy baseline to connect height, active work, speed, and launch angle.
Compare three cross-section families with a two-dimensional force ODE.
Add downhill slope as a third dimension and compare 25, 35, and 45 degree cases.
Use y and z exit velocities as proxies for vertical air.
Select z=0.07y^2-7 at 45 degrees for maximum and at 25 degrees for practicality.
task_reconstruction.coverage_note: The paper never computes the official vertical distance through a flight model, does not model twist, and defines the practical choice through unmodeled velocity conversion rather than an explicit tradeoff objective.

section_map.summary: States the three-model approach, candidate shapes, selected parabola and slopes, and 0.1 percent accuracy claim.
Defines half-pipe components, pumping, slope, vertical air, stunts, and practicality questions.
Previews conservation, two-dimensional ODE, and three-dimensional force models.
Derives passive speed, adds work, and discusses takeoff angle.
Defines drag, normal acceleration, and Cartesian force equations.
Rotates coordinates by mountain slope and adds downhill motion.
States constant pumping, no steering force, planar actuation, and no projectile motion.
Compares candidate cross-sections and reports exit velocity components.
Reports 45-degree component tables and percentage claims.
Names maximum and practical half-pipe scenarios.
Presents a marble analog and simulated trajectory image.
Lists invariant tests and asserts 0.1 percent RK4 error.
Suggests downhill cycloid, piecewise shapes, alternate work, and skilled-rider choices.
Prints parameters, piecewise derivatives, forces, RK4 state, and integration loop.
Provides domain sketches, scenario tables, and summary equations.
Lists mechanics, physics, sports, calculus, and web sources.

contributions.summary: Builds a clear progression from conservation to two-dimensional and three-dimensional dynamics.
Uses curvature-dependent normal loading to connect geometry with snow friction.
Attempts joint exploration of mountain slope and cross-pipe shape.
Constructs a bench half-pipe and compares marble motion with simulated displacement.
Uses conservative, damped, and phi=0 cases as internal model checks.
Publishes the RK4 code and parameter definitions rather than hiding the computational method.
Uses repeated consequences, strengths, and weaknesses sections to explain model escalation.

critical_dependency_failures: M1 adds dimensional work directly to speed squared without dividing by mass.
M2 and M3 do not enforce z=z(y) or compute the official projectile height.
C1 leaves y[4] and y[5] uninitialized, so its loop and downhill dynamics have undefined behavior.
C1 overwrites or omits piecewise derivatives and does not implement the declared pumping parameter.
R1 compares unmatched depths, endpoint angles, and cycle events.
R2 contains a prose-table ranking contradiction.
D1 relies on unmodeled conversion of downhill speed and no explicit practical objective.
V1 supplies no quantitative residuals and cannot validate a snowboarder model from a rolling marble.

assumptions.summary: Starts from rest and treats passive energy as gravity-only.
Uses one mass with no board flex, posture, rotation, or contact footprint.
Uses constant snow friction and quadratic air drag.
Represents rider pumping as one constant tangential force.
Excludes steering and direction-changing athlete force.
Applies added force only in the yz plane.
Assumes skilled riders can convert most downhill velocity into side-to-side velocity.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Uses two parabolas and a radius-10 circle over a common 20 m width but different depths and endpoint slopes.
Sets mass 75 kg, mu 0.04, air density 1.225, area 0.87, Cd 0.7, w 6000, and phi 15 degrees without parameter-specific evidence.
Reports shape, slope angle, cycle number, and y-z velocities but mixes event counts and zero outcomes.
Provides photographs but no scale, material, timing, trajectory, repeats, or calibration data.
Uses general mechanics and sports references but does not source the central pumping-force value.

models.summary: Correctly derives passive gravity speed but uses a dimensionally invalid active-work extension.
Combines gravity, normal acceleration, Coulomb friction, drag, and claimed pumping in Cartesian states.
Adds downhill slope through a rotated coordinate system and independent x dynamics.
Uses signed curvature radius to alter normal load and snow friction.
Separates x and yz losses rather than using vectors from total velocity and one contact force.
Intends two parabolic walls and a flat, but branch defects make slope and curvature undefined or wrong.
Implements a recognizable classical fourth-order update over six states.
Converts an unmodeled rider strategy and undefined velocity balance into a 25-degree recommendation.

verification.summary: Uses release-height conservation as a baseline invariant.
Checks perpetual oscillation after removing friction and drag.
Checks that passive dissipative motion comes to rest.
Checks that phi=0 reduces the three-dimensional model to two dimensions.
Compares a marble path and simulated path only visually.
Claims 0.1 percent RK4 error without a reference solution or convergence calculation.
Published code fails initialization, branch completeness, parameter-use, and paper-code parity checks.

results_trace.summary: Reports z=3.54291 m/s and y=2.527488 m/s for the shallow parabola.
Reports lower z components for the deeper parabola and circle under unmatched geometry.
Uses an unstated nonstandard denominator for the 23 percent claim.
Reports Parabola 1 with the largest y and z components at 45 degrees.
Contradicts the table by calling Parabola 2 44 percent better than Parabola 1.
Selects Parabola 1 at 45 degrees without computing vertical distance or landing.
Selects Parabola 1 at 25 degrees through unmodeled rider conversion and undefined evenness.
Reports 0.1 percent error without evidence and despite blocking code defects.

writing_logic.summary: Explains vertical, transition, flat, pumping, and downhill slope before modeling.
Previews how each model adds mechanisms and dimensions.
Uses consequences, strengths, and weaknesses after each model.
Reports results in the same baseline-to-2D-to-3D order as the methods.
Distinguishes mathematical maximum from practical recommendation but lacks a decision model.
Separates physical, computational, and analytical checks.
Makes implementation inspectable through code, figures, and equations.

language_observations.summary: States concrete results early but overstates model comprehensiveness and numerical accuracy.
Descriptive model names help readers track escalation.
Strengths and weaknesses headings encourage bounded claims.
Almost exactly mirrored is stronger than the unmeasured visual comparison supports.
Acceptable 0.1 percent is asserted without defining the error metric or reference.
The recommendation shifts from computed evidence to something to think about and unmodeled rider skill.

visualization_observations.summary: A simple energy diagram makes release height, coping height, speed, and angle intuitive.
The force overlay connects normal, gravity, and tangent motion to a real half-pipe profile.
A rotated-axis diagram clarifies the intended three-dimensional extension.
Before-and-after work trajectory plots are easy to compare but lack constraint residuals and unit-complete legends.
The three-dimensional path communicates downhill cycles but is difficult to read quantitatively.
The apparatus and simulation pairing is persuasive visually but has no registered overlay or residual.
Color-coded scenario tables are scannable but mix cycle events and unexplained zeros.
The compact result table omits cycle alignment, x speed, uncertainty, and scalar objective.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Official results verify Outstanding and MAA Award status but provide no causal commentary.
The accessible baseline-to-ODE-to-3D sequence may have appealed to mathematical exposition criteria.
The physical marble model may have made the solution memorable and visibly connected mathematics to reality.
Publishing a full code appendix and repeated self-critique may have outweighed severe implementation errors, but award status cannot prove this.

weaknesses.summary: Active work is added without division by mass.
Force and acceleration notation changes between body equations, appendix, and code.
rho is overloaded for curvature radius and active force.
Cartesian integration does not enforce the prescribed surface.
Drag and snow friction are not resolved from full three-dimensional velocity and contact.
The printed downhill equation contains a dimensional ma factor absent from code.
Projectile motion is omitted, so official vertical distance is never computed.
Shapes have different depth and endpoint angle.
The 23 percent denominator is unstated and nonstandard.
The 44 percent statement reverses the displayed Parabola 1 and Parabola 2 ordering.
Uses unmodeled speed conversion and undefined balance criteria.
No quantitative experiment-to-model comparison is supplied.
The 0.1 percent claim has no reference solution, norm, or convergence study.
States y[4] and y[5] are never initialized before use.
A second if overwrites left-wall curvature.
dzdy is uninitialized on the flat.
dzdy is overwritten with 0.5 and dz2dy remains uninitialized.
The w=6000 parameter is unused, so the shown solver has no pumping.
bob is computed but never used to check surface drift.
T_MAX, hi, and several initial-state macros are disconnected from execution.

independent_extensions.title: Code-first repair
independent_extensions.procedure: Initialize all states, replace branch logic with one total geometry function, enforce the surface constraint, compile with warnings and sanitizers, and regenerate all outputs.
independent_extensions.expected_gain: Removes undefined behavior and restores paper-code parity.

independent_extensions.title: Vector dynamics
independent_extensions.procedure: Use one global frame or explicit transforms, one contact-friction vector, one total-speed aerodynamic drag vector, and global vertical output.
independent_extensions.expected_gain: Corrects three-dimensional force direction and output semantics.

independent_extensions.title: Calibrated pumping
independent_extensions.procedure: Model bounded, phase-dependent athlete force or power and angular impulse using tracked-run calibration.
independent_extensions.expected_gain: Turns the central human mechanism into an auditable input.

independent_extensions.title: Matched geometry
independent_extensions.procedure: Compare curve families at common width, depth, coping angle, curvature, and construction constraints before varying one feature at a time.
independent_extensions.expected_gain: Separates shape effects from geometry confounders.

independent_extensions.title: Flight and landing
independent_extensions.procedure: Transform takeoff state to global coordinates and simulate projectile path, rotation, coping clearance, landing location, and impact load.
independent_extensions.expected_gain: Computes the official output and practical consequences.

independent_extensions.title: Quantitative analog validation
independent_extensions.procedure: Instrument and calibrate the bench course, track repeated marble trajectories, and report registered residuals and uncertainty.
independent_extensions.expected_gain: Preserves the paper's strong experimental instinct while making it evidentiary.

candidate_rule_impacts.summary: Creates a state-initialization, branch-totality, parameter-use, constraint, and paper-code parity gate for physical simulations.
Combines two 2011 half-pipe papers into a calibrated phase-dependent athlete-pumping rule.

unresolved_questions: Were the published tables generated by a different code version that initialized y[4]/y[5], repaired geometry branches, and used w?
What exact event defines the reported cycle velocity for each shape and why do 25-degree comparator rows remain zero?
How was the 0.1 percent RK4 error calculated?
What empirical basis supports the 6000 N pumping parameter and its duration?
What features did MAA judges explicitly cite? No reviewed official commentary answers this.
